Introduction

Pennsauken Municipal Court is a city courthouse in Camden County, New Jersey. It has jurisdiction over criminal and municipal violation cases and traffic and vehicle violations. It also handles speeding ticket matters received from the busy roadways 38, 90, and 130. It is a very busy court; they have handled almost 2000 criminal, and 35000 traffic charges form the last two years. Serious offenses are transferred to the Superior Court of Camden. The governing body of the town appointed the Clerk.

How can I take a virtual court session?

Pennsauken Municipal Court virtual court sessions were introduced in the era of Coronavirus by using the zoom application. A person can take the virtual court by submitting the virtual court session form. Fill in all the information required in the form and submit the request online. The court will review the application, and if your case is eligible for the online session, respond with a schedule and a zoom meeting link. It is recommended to join the meeting link 10 minutes before the actual time. Make sure you have a strong internet connection, and no noise occurs during the session; if you want to observe another person's virtual meeting, then join the link given on the website and watch it for your case guidance. The guidelines and answers to some questions related to this virtual session are available on the website; if you need help, you can download that document or contact the court.

How to find records information?

Pennsauken Municipal Court record information for cases are available in the town clerk's and county clerk's offices and found online on different websites. All the case information and trials are recorded and maintained by the county and Clerk's office. They can be searched online by using the following ways:

  • Searching by case number
  • Searching by name and city/state
  • Searching by address
  • Searching by phone
  • Searching by email

Sometimes, case information records are unavailable online because it is confidential according to the law. These types of information are only available at the county court or county clerk's office. They can be obtained by filing and sending a request form. Fill in all your personal information on the form. You had to describe in detail why you need these records. Send the fees for the copies of the record. After receiving the form, the court will either approve it or disapprove it and send it to the Clerk's office, and then Clerk will respond to you with the answer of the city council. For more information about the public records, call or mail the court. Read the information about the Open Public Record Act information for your guidance.

How to make a payment?

Pennsauken Municipal Court traffic tickets and other fines payments can be made in the following ways:

In-Person

A person can pay for tickets and fines by visiting the court during regular court hours and paying in cash, checks, or with a card at the court window. Take your ticket when you are coming for payment. 2.5% surcharges will be applied if you make payment with a credit card.

Online

Pennsauken Municipal Court online payment can be made using the New Jersey Online Payment Portal http://www.njmcdirect.com/. Enter the Ticket/Citation number or driver’s license number and enter search. Your case with the amount of the fine will be displayed. Select the payment option and pay the amount online. The service fees will be applied in this case.

Mail

A Person can send a certified check or money order to the court's mailing address, 2400 Bethel Ave, Pennsauken Township, NJ 08109, United States. Cash or personal checks are not acceptable in the mail; only certified checks or money orders are accepted. Remember to write your citation when you send the payment, and mail the amount in a self-addressed, stamped envelope if you want a receipt.

Which type of traffic cases are handled by this court?

Pennsauken Municipal Traffic court handles all traffic cases and violation that includes accident, hit and run, following someone very closely, speeding, driving while drinking or having drugs, driving carelessly or recklessly, failing to stop at the red sign, not following traffic rules, tailgating, driving with a suspended, expired or no license, and driving underage. In some traffic cases where the court appearance is checked, appearance in the court is mandatory; otherwise, write a plea and send it to the court. You can either write a plea of guilty if you accept your offense or not guilty if you do not accept your offense. If you write a plea of not guilty, then a trial date is given to you, and you must appear on the schedule with proof of your innocence. Consult or hire an attorney if you are writing a plea of not guilty and in those cases where your appearance is mandatory.

What are the functions of the Clerk?

Pennsauken Municipal Court clerk's function is to help the judges in the case, collect the payment of fines and traffic tickets, provides license, prepare agendas for the meetings, provides records of the open request form, solves and responds to all queries asked by the visitors but they cannot provides legal service. They are known as a custodian of all the municipality records and information.

How can I get a marriage license?

Pennsauken Municipal Court marriage license can be obtained from the Clerk's office and is provided by the Vital Statistics of the municipality. The fee for the license is $28. You had to come with your partner, fill out the marriage form, and provide any ID card that proves your identity with a birth certificate and a social security number. The couple must be 18+, and if the age is less than 18, the parent or guardian must be available when applying for the license. The marriage ceremony is performed at any court, district, or superior court judge.

Jurisdiction of the Pennsauken Municipal Court

The Pennsauken Municipal Court has jurisdiction over cases that occur within the geographical boundaries of Pennsauken Township. This includes cases that involve offenses committed on public roads, highways, and other public property within the township. Additionally, the court has jurisdiction over cases involving violations of Pennsauken Township ordinances, including but not limited to parking violations, noise violations, and zoning violations.

Procedures in the Pennsauken Municipal Court

If you receive a summons or a ticket from a Pennsauken Township police officer or code enforcement officer, you will likely be required to appear in the Pennsauken Municipal Court. The court is located at 2400 Bethel Avenue, Pennsauken, NJ 08109.

On the day of your court appearance, you should plan to arrive early to allow time for parking and security screening. You will be required to pass through a metal detector and have your bags searched before entering the courthouse. Once inside, you will need to check in with the court clerk and take a seat in the courtroom.

The court proceedings typically begin with the judge calling the docket, which is a list of all the cases scheduled for that day. When your case is called, you will be asked to approach the bench and stand before the judge. You will be required to swear or affirm that you will tell the truth, and then the judge will ask you to enter a plea of guilty or not guilty.

If you enter a plea of guilty, the judge will impose a sentence, which may include fines, community service, or other penalties. If you enter a plea of not guilty, the case will be scheduled for a trial, and you will have the opportunity to present your case before the judge.

Penalties for Pennsauken Municipal Court Offenses

The penalties for offenses in the Pennsauken Municipal Court vary depending on the nature and severity of the offense. For example, a first-time speeding offense may result in a fine of up to $200 and two points on your driver's license. A disorderly persons offense, such as disorderly conduct or harassment, may result in a fine of up to $1,000 and up to six months in jail.

It's important to note that the Pennsauken Municipal Court has the authority to impose penalties beyond fines and jail time. For example, the court may require you to perform community service, attend counseling or treatment programs, or comply with certain conditions of probation.

Navigating the Pennsauken Municipal Court System

If you are facing charges in the Pennsauken Municipal Court, it's important to understand your rights and legal options. Here are some tips for navigating the system:

  • Hire an experienced attorney: If you're facing serious charges, it's always advisable to hire an attorney who is familiar with the Pennsauken Municipal Court and its procedures. An experienced attorney can help you understand your legal options and build a strong defense on your behalf.
  • Understand the charges against you: Before you appear in court, it's essential to understand the nature of the charges against you and the potential penalties. This will help you prepare a defense and make informed decisions about your case.
  • Be respectful in court: When appearing in court, it's important to dress appropriately and be respectful to the judge, court staff, and other parties involved in your case. This can help to establish a positive impression and may work in your favor.
  • Be honest and cooperative: When appearing in court, it's essential to be honest and cooperative with the judge and court staff. Lying or being uncooperative can lead to additional charges and penalties.
  • Know your rights: You have the right to remain silent and the right to an attorney. If you are unsure about your legal rights, ask your attorney or the court staff for clarification.

By understanding the procedures and penalties of the Pennsauken Municipal Court, you can better navigate the system and protect your legal rights.

FAQ's

When will the court session hold?

Pennsauken Municipal Court session will be held every Tuesday at 8:00 pm and Thursday at 9:00 pm.

What is the dress code for this court during the hearing?

Proper and appropriate dressing is required during the court session hearing. Sleeveless, tight and torn are not allowed in this court.
